targetWords.definition: If someone is aggressive, then they constantly want to fight.
targetWords.example: •Nobody liked to play games with him because he was always too aggressive.

targetWords.definition: Amnesty is a pardon given to prisoners of war.
targetWords.example: She was denied amnesty for her involvement in the war.

targetWords.definition: An arena is a building where people can watch sports and concerts.
targetWords.example: •The new arena was all set to hold the championship match.

targetWords.definition: An auditorium is a large building used for public events.
targetWords.example: ■ People have gathered at the school auditorium to watch the play. captive [kaeptiv] n.

targetWords.definition: -* The guards told the captive that there was no way he could escape the prison.
targetWords.example: The guards told the captive that there was no way he could escape the prison.

targetWords.definition: Combat is fighting between two people or groups.
targetWords.example: The two warriors were locked in combat.

targetWords.definition: If something is commonplace, then it is ordinary.
targetWords.example: There is nothing commonplace about the way Morris dresses. compound [kampaund] n.

targetWords.definition: —► The workers waited outside the compound for the gates to the factory to open.
targetWords.example: The workers waited outside the compound for the gates to the factory to open. C o r p s [k o r] n.

targetWords.definition: —► The army had a corps of archers who trained apart from the regular soldiers.
targetWords.example: The army had a corps of archers who trained apart from the regular soldiers.

targetWords.definition: To distract someone means to stop them from concentrating on something.
targetWords.example: The phone call distracted him so much that he forgot all about his homework.

targetWords.definition: If someone is dumb, they are unable to speak.
targetWords.example: She did not share the secret. She remained silent as if she were dumb. foe [fou] n.

targetWords.definition: -+ It was hard to believe that anyone could be his foe.
targetWords.example: It was hard to believe that anyone could be his foe.

targetWords.definition: To hack something means to cut it into uneven pieces.
targetWords.example: My uncle used the ax to hack the tree into many logs.

targetWords.definition: To meditate means to focus or think deeply in silence.
targetWords.example: She liked to meditate for several hours of each day.

targetWords.definition: To nick someone means to cut them slightly with a sharp object.
targetWords.example: While cutting the carrots, the cook nicked his finger with the edge of his knife.

targetWords.definition: To provoke someone means to annoy them on purpose to cause violence.
targetWords.example: The older boy provoked Paul by calling him mean names. realm [relm] n.

targetWords.definition: —► He was not very active in the realm of business.
targetWords.example: He was not very active in the realm of business. reign [rein] n.

targetWords.definition: -» The emperor's reign lasted for only two years.
targetWords.example: The emperor's reign lasted for only two years.

targetWords.definition: Rust is a red and brown coating on iron objects caused by water and air.
targetWords.example: The old metal gate would not swing because the hinges were covered in rust.

targetWords.definition: If something is sacred, then it is worshipped and respected.
targetWords.example: One religion in India will not harm cows because it believes that they are sacred.

story.title: The Soldier's Decision
story.passage:
A soldier was captured while fighting in an enemy king's land. It was well known that

this king would make captives fight one another. This was commonplace during his reign.

For these fights, the king had built several large arenas. He often awarded the winners by

setting them free or even having them join his elite army corps.

The soldier, however, decided he had seen too much violence. He now felt that all life

was sacred. The night before his first match, he made a risky decision. He decided that he

would not engage in combat. He knew he may never be set free, but it was a decision that

he was willing to accept.

In the morning, he was led from the prisoners' compound to one of the king's arenas. A

gate coated in rust stood between him and the auditorium's floor. He was worried, but he

knew what he had to do.

When the gate opened, he calmly walked to the center of the arena and sat. He started

to meditate. His foe Darius, who was skilled in the realm of sword fighting and was typically

not very aggressive, would not fight the quiet soldier until he attacked Darius first.

Darius tried to provoke him by hacking at the air close to his head with his sword. But

the soldier was not distracted. He sat quietly, as if he were dumb, and looked calmly up at

the sky. Even when Darius nicked him on the cheek with the edge of his sword, the soldier

did not move.

At last he threw down his sword and shield and gave up.

"I can't fight someone who refuses to fight me!" Darius

shouted to the king.

The king was very impressed with the soldier.

Never in any battle had he seen someone so

brave. As a result, he gave the peaceful soldier

amnesty. The soldier's actions proved to the king

and everyone in the arena that peace was more

powerful than fighting.
